title: Regional warm-start probe + priority-aware dampening to stabilize autoscaling during multi-region failover
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: During cross-region failover events we observe a cascade: readiness probes flip to unhealthy while new capacity cold-starts, autoscaler interprets transient failures as sustained unhealthy signals, and aggressive scale-up/scale-down churn occurs. This leads to SLO breaches (p99 latency spikes, increased error rate) for enterprise customers with multi-region routing.

Goal: Implement a two-part system: 1) regional warm-start probes that exercise a light-weight warmup path (KV cache prefetch + small model shard warmup) before declaring a node ready; 2) priority-aware probe dampening that increases probe hysteresis for low-priority tokens/requests while keeping fast paths for high-priority traffic. Together these should reduce autoscaler thrash and keep p99 latency within SLO during failover drills.

Scope: design and implement probe types, autoscaler integration for dampening decisions, metrics and dashboards, e2e chaos tests, and staged rollout to Dedicated clusters in us-west-2 and eu-central-1.
acceptance_criteria:
- Simulated region failover test (see test plan) shows p99 tail latency stays within SLO (<= 350ms for small-model gen workloads) and overall error rate does not exceed historical baseline+0.5% during failover window.
- Autoscaler scale events reduced: reduction of scale-up/scale-down cycles during failover by >= 50% compared to baseline measured in previous incident (incident-2026-01-17).
- New probe types exposed via runtime flags and feature-gated in Console.
- Documentation and runbook published, and on-call runbook includes clear rollback steps.
- Canary rollout completed to 10% of Dedicated clusters with no regressions for 72 hours.
design_notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs considered: 
1) Warm-start probe actions: keep probes cheap (~<20ms) — prefetch only top-3 KV prefixes used for typical prefixes and perform a lightweight conv-kernel warmup for the model shard. Avoid full model initialization in probe path to prevent probe itself causing slow startups.
2) Dampening policy: avoid global static hysteresis. Use request-priority tag (from token metadata) to choose hysteresis window: high-priority requests get short hysteresis (fast readiness), low-priority requests get extended hysteresis to avoid noisy signals. This requires propagating priority into health streams.
3) Autoscaler integration: introduce a probe-confidence score fused with existing health metrics (CPU, memory, queue length). Score in [0..100] and autoscaler will ignore readiness flips while score < threshold for N seconds.
4) Backward compatibility: default behavior disabled and backwards-compatible flags added. Operators can tune thresholds per-cluster.

Open questions: 
- How to safely surface request priority from external LB without adding latency? (edge hook vs token metadata)
- What default thresholds to ship for mixed workloads? Proposed: conservative defaults tuned from chaos runs.

Related artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Regional+Warm-Start+Probes (draft), PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4928
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind 'regional-warmstart' and 'priority-dampening'.
2) Unit + integration tests in CI; runbook prepared.
3) Canary: enable on 1 cluster in us-west-2 for low-load traffic (10% of Dedicated clusters) for 72h. Monitor dashboards and on-call alerts.
4) If stable, expand to 3 clusters (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-central-1).
5) Full rollout to Dedicated clusters after 2 weeks of stable canary and SLO verification.
6) Monitor for unexpected degradation for another 30 days; if detected, roll back feature flags.

Rollback criteria: increase in p99 latency > 20% or sustained error-rate +1% above baseline for 10 minutes.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for probe code paths and priority propagation.
- Integration test: bootstrap a node with warm-start probe enabled and validate probe does not cause full model init and that readiness is delayed until KV prefetch succeeds.
- Chaos test: simulate network partition and regional failover in staging; compare autoscaler events, readiness flips, and p99 between baseline and feature-on.
- Load test: replay production traces with blended priorities to ensure low-priority dampening doesn't starve important traffic.
- Observability: add probe_confidence metric, probe_latency histogram, and a 'probe_cause' tag for readiness events.

Test artifacts: load harness job id: job/ci/warmstart-2026-03-01, chaos script: gs://redwood-testing/chaos/warmstart-failover-v1
metrics:
Primary: p99 latency for small-gen workloads; readiness flip rate per-node; autoscaler events per-minute; error-rate.
Secondary: probe_latency_ms p95, probe_confidence distribution, cold-start duration percentiles.
Targets: decrease readiness flip rate by >=50% during failover window; autoscaler events per-minute <= baseline*0.5; probe latency p95 < 50ms in steady state.
